subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: Invisible Man and Black Identity
description: Learn Invisible Man and Black Identity in one minute.

hook.text: Ralph Ellison spent seven years writing a novel about a man nobody could see, not because of magic but racism.

buildup.text: Invisible Man followed an unnamed Black narrator navigating a society that refused to see him as a person.

discovery.text: Published in 1952, it won the National Book Award and outsold every other novel that year.

twist.text: Some Black critics attacked the novel, saying it was too complex and not politically direct enough.

climax.text: The novel redefined how American literature explored race, identity, and the meaning of visibility.

punchline.text: An invisible man became impossible to ignore.

quiz.question: Why is the narrator of Invisible Man invisible?
options: Society refuses to see him as a person because of racism
